name: Opaque 40-character installation token
description: The stateful installation token GitHub issued before the stateless rollout: ghs_ followed by an opaque body with no dots, described by the provider as 40 characters long (ghs_ plus 36). The provider says existing tokens of this kind keep working until they expire and that a temporary request header can still ask for this form during the rollout, so the form is still observable. GitHub's 2026-10-02 entry makes the stateless form the default for new tokens and sets 2026-11-30 as the date the header stops being respected; whether the opaque form is issued at all after that is not stated.

history.note: From 2026-04-27 GitHub began issuing the stateless form to newly minted installation tokens in a staged rollout; this opaque form stays valid for tokens already issued and can be requested with the disabled header value. No retirement date is stated, so this is recorded as revised, not retired.

sources.supports: Staged rollout from 2026-04-27 changes the format of newly minted installation tokens; existing tokens continue to work until they expire; applications that rely on exactly 40 characters may break.
The header value disabled returns a stateful (classic opaque) token even if the integration is already in the rollout.

history.note: GitHub stated on 2026-10-02 that by default all newly minted installation tokens are now stateless, so this opaque form is no longer the default for new tokens; tokens minted earlier work until they expire (they last one hour), and the disabled header value is described as returning this form until the header is deprecated on 2026-11-30, after which all eligible apps always receive stateless tokens. No source read says whether the opaque form is issued at all after that date, so this is recorded as revised, not retired.

sources.supports: Default for newly minted tokens is now stateless; earlier tokens work until they expire; one-hour expiration unchanged; header deprecated 2026-11-30 with all eligible apps then always receiving stateless tokens.
sources.locator: What's changed; What to expect going forward

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. The 40-character figure is stated by the provider as an assumption applications must not rely on; the 36-character body and the CRC32 checksum remain in contract revision 1.
